chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn 'Abdus, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Abi Jamilah, from al-Asbagh, from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, who said:
The hand is not cut off for one who steals something from fruit; and if he passes by it, then let him eat, but let him not spoil [it].

key_terms.لَا يُفْسِدْ: he must not damage, waste, or spoil
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: the legal cutting off of the hand as a hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd punishment applied for stealing fruit, and may a passerby eat from it without causing damage?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that the hadd punishment of amputation does not apply to one who steals some fruit. It also permits a passerby to eat from fruit when passing by, on condition that he does not cause damage or spoil it.
